topics.title: Roman Space Telescope launches
topics.summary: NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida, sending a powerful wide-field observatory toward deep-space surveys of planets, galaxies, dark matter, and dark energy.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio got a telescope that could scan huge chunks of space, who would look for aliens first and who would use it to find missing props?

topics.title: Nepal issues new flood alerts
topics.summary: Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding after a Himalayan glacial collapse devastated border communities, damaged roads and power plants, and left rescue teams racing difficult terrain.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone had to pack one practical thing for a community emergency kit, what would each character insist was absolutely essential?

topics.title: Zaporizhzhia runs on generators
topics.summary: Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant remained cut off from external power, with the UN nuclear watchdog pushing for repairs while emergency diesel generators keep safety systems running.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who in the studio would be best at calmly managing backup power, and who would immediately label every switch with dramatic names?

topics.title: Iran war reshapes costs
topics.summary: AP reports the six-month Iran war has created uneven economic effects: markets recovered, oil-linked costs rose, and poorer countries face extra pressure from fuel and fertilizer prices.
topics.discussionPrompt: If prices changed around the studio overnight, what would everyone try to save money on first: travel, food, gadgets, or the coffee budget?

topics.title: Venezuela oil deal debated
topics.summary: President Trump announced a U.S.-Venezuela oil access deal, but analysts warned the fields need major investment and many details about operators and funding remain unclear.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio suddenly inherited a huge resource, who would ask the careful questions and who would already be designing merch?

topics.title: Canada trade leverage questioned
topics.summary: CBC reported economists see Canada holding leverage in its trade fight with the U.S., while warning that using it could still bring costs for households and businesses.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had leverage in a negotiation, who would play it cool and who would accidentally reveal the whole strategy over lunch?

topics.title: Datacenter fights gain attention
topics.summary: The Guardian highlighted how local opposition to AI datacenters is becoming a broader political issue, with communities focused on power use, water demands, and decision-making.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a giant datacenter wanted to move next door, what would the characters ask for in return: cheaper power, jobs, quiet, or snacks?

topics.title: Women in arts report released
topics.summary: A new UK arts report said many women still feel they lack equal opportunities, with age bias and unconscious sexism cited as barriers in creative careers.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had to make auditions feel fairer, what rule would each character add to keep the room honest and relaxed?

topics.title: Tampa ballpark plan advances
topics.summary: Tampa approved a $2.3 billion plan for a new Rays ballpark and entertainment district, with county officials still expected to weigh in on the project.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio got to design a ballpark district, what would be the must-have attraction besides the game itself?

topics.title: Germany far-right symbols scrutinized
topics.summary: CBC reported researchers are tracking how coded far-right symbols are appearing more openly in Germany as political support for the movement grows.
topics.discussionPrompt: How would the characters handle spotting a symbol they do not understand: research it, ask someone, ignore it, or turn it into a mystery board?
